# Project Vision

This project builds a fully reproducible, query-driven hydrothermal system platform for Steamboat Springs.

The system integrates:

- field sampling
- NDEP regulatory chemistry
- NDWR hydrologic data (wells + water levels)
- continuous temperature sensors
- laboratory analyses
- isotope datasets (future)
- geochemical modeling outputs (PHREEQC)

All data are stored in a single relational database and accessed through derived views and analysis workflows.

---

# Core Design Philosophy

## Single Source of Truth

All raw data are stored in one SQLite database:

database/geochem_operational.sqlite

This database contains:

- normalized tables
- enforced relationships
- reproducible ingest pipelines

---

## Layered Architecture

The system is structured into three layers:

RAW TABLES
- original ingested data
- never modified after ingestion

DERIVED VIEWS
- computed and cleaned datasets
- reusable across analysis and GIS

ANALYSIS AND EXPORT
- R scripts perform computation
- RMarkdown produces reports
- GeoPackage exports deliver GIS-ready layers

---

## Separation of Responsibilities

Database:
- stores all raw and derived data

Ingest scripts:
- load and standardize external datasets

Views:
- define analysis-ready datasets

R scripts:
- perform calculations (gradients, mixing, etc.)

RMarkdown:
- visualization and interpretation

GeoPackage:
- GIS-ready outputs

PHREEQC (future):
- geochemical modeling layer

---

## Modular Expansion

New data types are added through:

- new tables for raw data
- new views for derived results
- new scripts for analysis

---

# Hydrologic System (NDWR Wells)

## Structure

Wells table defines physical wells  
Water_Level_Observations stores time-series measurements  
Locations provides spatial reference  

---

## Analysis Views (Core Hydro Layer)

vw_hydraulic_head
- computes hydraulic head from depth-to-water
- includes measurement method flags
- primary dataset for flow analysis

vw_water_level_latest
- most recent measurement per well
- used for mapping water table surface

vw_water_level_daily_best
- one measurement per well per day
- prioritizes manual measurements over sensors

vw_hydraulic_head_clean
- filtered dataset using only high-quality measurements
- used for gradient analysis and modeling

vw_wells_gis
- GIS-ready well dataset
- includes depth classification

---

## Capabilities Now Available

- hydraulic head calculation
- cleaned time-series
- map-ready groundwater surfaces
- well characterization

---

# Analysis Workflow

## Structure

Database views provide input  
R scripts compute results  
RMarkdown produces outputs  

---

## Components

Views:
- reusable datasets

R scripts:
- located in scripts/analysis
- perform calculations

RMarkdown:
- located in analysis/
- produces figures and reports

---

## Key Rule

RMarkdown should not contain heavy computation.  
All computation should occur in views or scripts.

# ============================================================
# Latest Update — 06/05/2026
# Major System Milestone Achieved ✅
# ============================================================

## 🚀 Achievements in Current Session

This session completed the transition from a data ingestion project to a fully operational hydroinformatics system.

---

### ✅ End-to-End Pipeline Stabilized

The system now successfully executes:

- ingestion → database → views → analysis → QC → GIS export

All components are:

- deterministic
- reproducible
- internally consistent

---

### ✅ Hydraulic Gradient System (Complete)

Status: ✅ Fully implemented

Capabilities:

- spatial pairing of wells using projected coordinates (UTM)
- distance-based filtering to prevent combinatorial explosion
- gradient magnitude calculation (Δh / distance)
- flow direction (azimuth in degrees)
- classification into low / moderate / high gradients

Key Outputs:

- `Hydraulic_Gradients` (materialized table)
- `vw_hydraulic_gradients` (view)
- GeoPackage line layer

Design Improvements:

- stable coordinate system (EPSG:32611)
- efficient filtering prior to geometry generation
- scalable to large datasets (>600k pairs handled)

---

### ✅ Geometry & GIS Export System (Major Breakthrough)

Status: ✅ Fully operational

Resolved complex issues:

- WKB vs EWKB incompatibility
- SQLite geometry storage limitations
- `sf` parsing failures
- GeoPackage write constraints for large datasets

Final Design Pattern:

- geometry stored in database (non-authoritative)
- geometry reconstructed or validated during export
- GeoPackage outputs always valid and GIS-ready

Enhancements:

- gradient layer filtering (distance + magnitude)
- export row cap (100k features) for performance
- coordinate extraction from vector geometry

---

### ✅ QA/QC Framework (Operational)

Status: ✅ Implemented

Checks include:

- missing spatial coordinates
- orphaned records
- gradient outliers
- temperature anomalies
- invalid chemistry values
- duplicate samples

Outputs:

- database summary table (`QC_Summary`)
- CSV reports in `output/qc/`

Design philosophy:

- non-destructive
- transparent
- reproducible

---

### ✅ Chemistry System Expansion

Status: ✅ Stable

New capabilities:

- unified chemistry via `vw_sample_master`
- major ions extraction (`vw_major_ions`)
- isotope GIS layer (`vw_isotopes_gis`)

Supports:

- spatial visualization
- future mixing analysis
- geochemical modeling

---

### ✅ Deterministic View Layer (Critical Upgrade)

All views now:

- are rebuilt every run (`DROP + CREATE`)
- act as schema contracts
- guarantee reproducibility

Eliminates:

- stale views
- schema drift
- inconsistent downstream analysis

---

### ✅ GeoPackage Export (Production Ready)

Location:
output/geopackage/hydro_data.gpkg

Now includes:
